title: The middle way
intro: Islam teaches balance: not going to extremes, and giving everything its right.

learn.html: Every day in Salah we ask Allah to guide us to the Straight Path – the basic condition for a successful life in this world. Staying on the Straight Path means keeping to the middle way. In the Qur’an, Allah described Muslims as a people of the middle, of moderation and balance.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah tells us that He made the Muslims a just, balanced community, so that they would be witnesses over people, and the Messenger a witness over them. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:143)</small>

The middle way means looking for the middle and the balance between two opposite extremes. It is the way of keeping balance so that neither side wins, and following what is most valuable, most just, best and most complete.

Following the middle way and being balanced in practising the religion and in life is very important for the unity, harmony and peace of the community. The middle way puts nobody below others and gives everyone the right they deserve in the community.
Islam teaches, raises and guides Muslims not to go to extremes, but to keep to the middle way – the way walked by those Allah is pleased with and to whom He gave His blessings.

learn.title: 1. This world and the next
learn.html: Islam asks us to work and earn for this world and to provide for ourselves and our family, but it also asks us to strive for the eternal life to come.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Seek, through what Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter, but do not forget your share of this world, and do good to others as Allah has done good to you. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Qasas 28:77)</small>

learn.title: 2. Me and the community
learn.html: Islam calls us to hold firmly to the community and to be its most useful members. At the same time, it asks us to give time to our family and to our own health. So we need to find a balance between both duties.

practice.title: Extreme or the middle way?
practice.prompt: Is this the middle way or going to an extreme?

items.text: Praying all five prayers on time and also doing homework and playing
Working and earning, and also remembering the Hereafter
Helping in the community and also spending time with family
Thinking only about money and forgetting Salah
Praying only sometimes, when you feel like it
Staying in the masjid all day and never helping your family

practice.prompt: Tap every true sentence, then tap Check.

options.text: Looking for balance between two extremes
Giving everyone the right they deserve

options.why: The middle way is not praying sometimes – we pray all our prayers regularly.
Islam asks us to work for this world and also for the Hereafter.
